# `←` — Assign

`N←Y` binds a name to an array, function or operator. Chained assignment returns the assigned value silently.

```bpl
x←3 ⋄ x+2          ⍝ 5
sum←+/ ⋄ sum1 2 3 ⍝ 6
```

`←` binds tightly on its left and loosely on its right. The target is the run immediately before `←`: a name, a dot path such as `x.[1]`, or a group. The value is everything to its right, so spaces there group runs as usual.

```bpl
x←1+2 × 3 ⋄ x      ⍝ 9
```

`N f←Y` updates with `N f Y`. A named function goes in parentheses, `N(f)←Y`, because a space would end the run that holds the target. A [dot index](dot.qmd) is a selective target. `x.[1]←9` updates item 1 through [Index](squad.qmd) `⌷`. Other selections need parentheses: `(f N)←Y` updates the items that `f` selects.

```bpl
x←10 ⋄ x+←3 ⋄ x    ⍝ 13
f←× ⋄ x←3 ⋄ x(f)←4 ⋄ x ⍝ 12
x←1 2 3 ⋄ x.[[0 2]]+←10 ⋄ x ⍝ 11 2 13
x←1 2 3 ⋄ x.[1]←9 ⋄ x ⍝ 1 9 3
x←1 2 3 ⋄ (2↑x)←8 9 ⋄ x ⍝ 8 9 3
```

Brackets destructure: each name gets the corresponding item.

```bpl
[a b]←10 20 ⋄ a+b  ⍝ 30
```

Independent assignments need `⋄`, as in `a←1 ⋄ b←2`.

Inside dfns, plain assignment is local. Modified and selective array updates target the nearest existing binding. Arrays have value semantics.
